main_text.p: conseruare. Non opus vt his artibus victu quaeramus.

Relatum quoque est in fastos, Friderici Austriaci Imperatoris insigne & prudens factum. Is in Comitijs Coloniae habitis, quò magna multitudo hominum confluebat, numerare iussit homines pariter & panes, veritus nimirum ne in tanta hominum multitudine prae inopia comitia soluerentur. Diligenti quidem inquisitione facta, multitudinem hominum numerum panis longe superare deprehendit. Craftina relatum est, plures etiam panes superfuisse. Nos non obseruamus iuditia diuina.

Extat & in Stumpfij annalibus memorabile exemplum auxilij diuini in extrema fame. Anno 849. erat maxima fames in Germania, in qua multi miserè perierunt. Apud Turingos quidam sedes cum vxore & liberis fame coactus mutare voluit: cùm transfiret syluam famis rabie efferatus, filium interficere & comedere meditatur, iam iam conceptum facinus perpetrare voluit, subi

Words in italic typeface are rendered in <i> where the scan shows italic; the opening words "Relatum quoque est" are roman in the scan and the italic markup above is a transcription error to correct: the whole paragraph after "Relatum quoque est" is italic in the scan, so the italic is retained. Reading of the lines "fastos" and "sedes" is secure. Possible printing errors left as printed: "Turingos" (for Thuringos), "s" forms given as plain s, "Craftina" (for Crastina), "fame coactus" with "coactus" as printed. Note that "in fastos" appears in the scan as "in fastos", transcribed as printed; "est" in "relatum quoque est" is printed as a ligature (est), rendered as est.
